'''EPP Overdrive''' is a fast sealed deck format played with one [[Enhanced Premiere]] pack (EPP) per player, 30-card decks and 15-minute games. [[Decipher]] introduced it as "the newest sanctioned Sealed Deck tournament format", and the [[Players Committee]]'s ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' (revised September 2015) keeps it.<ref name="dec-epp">[http://tournaments.decipher.com/eppoverdriveformat.asp EPP Overdrive Sealed Deck Format], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020220230930/http://tournaments.decipher.com/eppoverdriveformat.asp Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''Type:''' sealed deck
* '''Defined by:''' Decipher (by February 2002); Players Committee (2015)
* '''Card pool:''' one Enhanced Premiere pack per player, 30-card decks
* '''In use:''' by 2002 &ndash; listed in 2015
* '''GEMP:''' none

== Card pool ==
Each player starts with one Enhanced Premiere pack. Decipher strongly recommended the [[Darth Vader With Lightsaber]] pack for Dark Side decks and the [[Luke With Lightsaber]] pack for Light Side decks, but any EPP of the right side works. Tournament directors provide equal numbers of Dark and Light packs.<ref name="dec-epp" />

Decipher's rules:<ref name="dec-epp" />
* The field is split into equal groups of Dark and Light players. With an odd number, one player of the larger side gets a bye in the first game; later byes go to the lowest-rated player of that side who has not had one.
* The deck building phase is 15 minutes, timed strictly. Opponents sit across from each other, open their packs, and give each other the cards of the opposite side face down. Each player builds a 30-card deck.
* A deck may be tweaked only with cards left over from the player's own pack; no trading.
* Games have a 15-minute limit. A game that runs over is scored as a modified win: 1 victory point plus Life Force for the winner, 0 victory points minus that differential for the loser.
* Sanctioning required at least 3 games; 4 to 6 were recommended.

The Players Committee guide runs EPP Overdrive under its general sealed rules with the same product, recommended packs, 30-card decks, 15-minute games and 15-minute deck building, and asks for a minimum of 4 games.<ref name="afg" />

== History ==
Decipher's page called EPP Overdrive "a fast-moving alternative to the typical four-hour event".<ref name="dec-epp" /> The earliest preserved copy of the page is from 20 February 2002; when Decipher first posted it is unknown. In August 2002 Decipher's Star Wars tournament resources page listed "EPP Overdrive Sealed Deck Format" among its format notes.<ref name="dec-ressw">[http://tournaments.decipher.com/resources-sw.asp Star Wars tournament resources], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020808154840/http://tournaments.decipher.com/resources-sw.asp Internet Archive].</ref> The 2015 Players Committee guide names EPP Overdrive as the one exception to its rule of one minute of game time per card.<ref name="afg" />
